purpose: Define the Git-only source-trust contract used by version-1 durable releases. It turns the approved source commit into freshly observed, non-durable trust evidence that is re-observed before every effect.
scope: Fresh Git observation, canonical workspace-root binding, clean detached-HEAD policy, and re-observation rules. This does not define release policy, durable intent fields, graph preparation, provider effects, or a non-Git release mode.
non_goals: Supporting branch, symbolic-HEAD, dirty-worktree, non-Git, HermeticContent, or SHA-256 Git-object-format execution in version 1.
Using a Git SHA as evidence of human authorship, signature verification, or forge authorization.
Persisting a workspace path, raw git output, remote URL, or arbitrary Git diagnostic in a durable intent, state, receipt, or artifact manifest.
A local workspace release lock; re-observing Git state before every effect is the guard against workspace changes.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Version-1 authorization starts from a caller-supplied workspace root, canonicalizes that root, discovers the Git repository containing it, and rejects a root that does not resolve to that repository's worktree root. The observed identity is the exact full CommitSha at HEAD; it is never supplied by a CLI flag, inferred from a branch name, or obtained from a remote ref. The private trust evidence binds the canonical root and observed commit together.

[UPDATED 2026-09-24] Version 1 accepts only a SHA-1 Git repository at the exact 40-hex GitCommit SourceIdentity in the received ReleaseIntentV1. The detached-HEAD-only requirement is scoped to the CI route (`ReleaseCheckout::Detached`, crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/capability.rs:227-235); the local `callisto release` route (`validate_local_release_intent`, `ReleaseCheckout::AnyHead`, capability.rs:324, crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/local.rs:260-291) accepts a branch checkout. It rejects SHA-256 Git-object-format repositories, an absent/unresolvable HEAD, a non-canonical or non-equal commit, and a shallow/incomplete checkout when the required commit or tag inspection cannot be performed; on the CI route only, a symbolic HEAD is also rejected even when it currently resolves to the same commit. Equality uses CommitSha values, never prefix or raw-string comparison.

Authorization requires a clean worktree before the capability is issued. 'Clean' means Git status, queried without ignored entries, reports no staged, unstaged, unmerged, or untracked file under the repository worktree. Every path the repository's ignore rules exclude, such as build output, is allowed and never blocks; there is no fixed ignored-path allowlist. A tracked modification or an untracked non-ignored file fails closed with a diagnostic naming its relative path. A path outside the canonical root, an error while determining status, or an ambiguous repository layout fails closed. Diagnostics do not retain raw command output in durable data.

The release executor re-observes the same canonical root, detached HEAD, clean-worktree status, and exact approved commit immediately before every remote or VCS effect. A change after authorization blocks the next effect.

The trust API is a read-only callisto-vcs surface returning closed, typed GitCommitTrustEvidence values. It does not depend on callisto-graph, callisto-cli, forge SDKs, or registry clients. Its errors derive miette::Diagnostic with stable codes and remediation, and its durable-facing output contains only validated typed identities rather than shell text.

Tests cover non-Git roots, nested/non-root invocation, symbolic HEAD, dirty tracked and untracked worktrees, commit mismatch, and a mutation between authorization and an effect-time recheck. Tests assert that each failure occurs before an effect adapter is invoked.

implementation_notes: GitAccess (the sole shell-backed Git type since f3b1c1bcf dropped GitRepository/ShellGit/GitDataSource) should expose structured observation rather than making graph parse porcelain or command text. The existing CommitSha type is the equality boundary.
A future closed-root byte observer may add HermeticContent under a separate schema/profile version. It must not weaken the GitCommit behavior specified here.
reasoning: A Git commit only becomes a release trust boundary when the executor proves it is operating at the approved checkout. Mandatory fresh observation before every effect preserves correctness when another tool changes the workspace.
